acme-corp-support: Hey team — customers on our retail integration are seeing intermittent 429s since ~03:20 UTC. ~8-12% of requests return 429, no obvious client change. Posting a couple request IDs we captured: req_79a2, req_c3f1, req_d4e5. Any quick repro steps we can ask them to run?

maria: Thanks — can you confirm whether those IDs come with X-Rate-Limit headers? Also which endpoint and model? If you can paste one raw request/response (headers) that helps.

acme-corp-support: Endpoint is POST /v1/generate (model=gpt-neo-35) from a pool of 6 clients behind a single NAT. We grabbed one response head:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 03:20:45 GMT
x-request-id: req_79a2
x-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 26
content-type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}
```

sam: Good, that header set looks like a standard token-bucket hit. Remaining=0 and reset=26 (secs) means they hit a short window. Two quick asks to repro: 1) please replay a single client at high QPS with the same Authorization header and include `-H "X-Request-ID: <id>"` so our logs match, 2) capture a HAR or `curl --trace-ascii` output for a failing request.

alex: Also helpful: run this quick curl that forces the same payload/headers so we can reproduce from our side:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_replay_test_01" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-35","input":"test"}' \
  --compressed --connect-timeout 5 -v
```

lisa: If they can run the above in a tight loop (100 req/s) for 30s from the same IP, that'll show whether it's a short bucket burst vs a sustained policy. Ask them to include timestamps and the X-Request-ID values for failing requests.

acme-corp-support: Can also confirm they observed a pattern where spikes happen at :20 and :50 each minute. We think it's their job scheduler causing a burst. We'll try the loop now and post results + HAR.

maria: Perfect. When you post the HAR/trace, include at least three failing X-Request-ID values and the client IPs if possible. We'll pull matching traces on our side. I'll also trigger a quick quota audit for that org (cc @alex).

acme-corp-support: Posting first batch: req_79a2 (03:20:45Z), req_c3f1 (03:20:46Z), req_d4e5 (03:20:46Z). Attaching a small HAR and a `--trace-ascii` dump to the ticket. HAR shows requests back-to-back from same source NAT.

sre-bot: Created ticket RED-2891 and attached logs from edge-01 for times 03:20:30-03:21:10. Preliminary: saw 85 429s from that org, source IP x.x.142.12, average latency 120ms.

sam: Thanks — next steps for support: 1) gather the customer's HAR + trace, 2) get client pid/job schedule that could cause bursts, 3) confirm whether they share tokens among many clients (that changes per-key throttling). For eng-sre: can you check whether rate-limiter experienced any short pathological queueing at 03:20?

alex: I'll pull limiter metrics and per-tenant token bucket traces for that window and reply with a short timeline here. If it's quota exhaustion we can propose a short-Term increase or recommend spreading jitter.

acme-corp-support: Uploading HAR now, will try the curl loop and paste results in thread in ~10m. Thanks all :pray:
